check_cves.description: Take a list of CVE IDs, such as the findings of a scanner, and get back which of them CISA has confirmed are being exploited. Those are the ones to fix first. The answer separates the listed CVEs (in full) from the ones that are not listed, counts how many have known ransomware use, and sets a flag a workflow can branch on, so nothing fails just because a CVE is absent. No API key required.

listed.vulnerability_name: Apache Log4j2 Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

parameters.description: How to order the entries. Newest added first by default.
parameters.name: sort

parameters.description: How many entries to return. The answer also carries the total number that matched, so a capped list never reads as a complete one.

parameters.name: offset

truncated.description: True when matches were left out by the limit.

search_vulnerabilities.description: Search the catalog for a word, phrase, CVE ID or product name and get the best matches first. A hit on the CVE ID outranks one on the vulnerability name, which outranks the vendor or product, which outranks the description and the advisory notes, and each result says which fields it matched on. Use it when you have a term rather than a filter. No API key required.

description: Work with the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog: the US government's authoritative list of the vulnerabilities attackers are actually exploiting. Check a scanner's findings or your software inventory against it, browse and search it by vendor, product, weakness type or date, see what CISA added this week, track remediation deadlines, pull out the ones used in ransomware campaigns, and export any of it as CSV. No account or API key required.
